name: matcha-5198d8f0-blind30
instr:
# matcha-regen

This is a terminal mail program, and someone who uses it every day wrote down what went
wrong over a few days of ordinary use. Nothing about their mail accounts changed and
nothing about the servers changed.
The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.
What follows is everything that was noticed from the outside.

Starting it from a shell is already odd. Invoked with a tracing switch and the switch that
turns on the pane showing recent activity, both ahead of a version request, it leaves that
pane off and hands onward an argument list that is not the one typed; giving a subcommand
its own pane switch has that switch swallowed and mistaken for the global pane request,
with the leftovers again altered, as though the walk over the leading arguments were
shifted by one position.

Accounts do not survive being written and read back. Saving a set of them and loading them
straight away yields accounts that are not equal to what was saved: the password is never
filled in on reload, so an account whose password is meant to come from running a small
shell command that prints the secret comes back with an empty password, even though the
command text itself is on disk and still there afterwards. Deleting one of two accounts
then mangles the stored address book, keeping the entry that only the deleted account had
used and dropping the entry both accounts shared, exactly the opposite fate for each,
although the mail, folder and draft data kept for the account
